messages.content: 我正在计划一次露营旅行，我需要知道天气预报。你能帮我获取下一个10天内，位于纬度、经度-121.34的露营地点的天气数据吗？包括每日的温度和降水预报。同时，我更希望温度以华氏度的2分钟最高值给出，降水量以英寸为单位的总和。

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.reasoning:
The user wants weather forecast for next 10 days at latitude unspecified? They said "位于纬度、经度-121.34的露营地点". That seems incomplete: they gave only longitude -121.34 but not latitude. We need both lat and lon. So we must ask clarifying question: what is the latitude? Also they want temperature as Fahrenheit 2-minute maximum values? Actually they say "温度以华氏度的2分钟最高值给出". That might mean they want daily max temperatures in Fahrenheit. And precipitation sum in inches.

We can use Open-Meteo API. It supports hourly and daily forecasts. For daily max temp, we can get daily variable "temperature_2m_max" which returns max over day. Units default to Celsius. We can set units=imperial to get Fahrenheit. Precipitation total daily is "precipitation_sum" in mm. We can convert to inches: 1 inch = 25.4 mm. But maybe Open-Meteo supports unit conversion via parameter "timezone" and "units"? I think units param can be "si" or "us". Setting units=us will give temperature in Fahrenheit and precipitation in inches? Let's check: According to Open-Meteo docs, units=us gives temperature in Fahrenheit, windspeed in mph, precipitation in inches. Yes.

So we can call the API with params: latitude=?, longitude=-121.34, daily=["temperature_2m_max", "precipitation_sum"], timezone="auto", units="us", start_date=today, end_date=+9 days? Actually we need next 10 days inclusive? We'll fetch 10 days including today? Or next 10 days after today? Probably next 10 days starting tomorrow. We'll compute dates accordingly.

But we don't have latitude. So we must ask for latitude. Also we need to confirm if they want daily max temperature and daily precipitation sum. They mention "2分钟最高值" maybe misinterpretation. But likely they want daily max temperature. We'll clarify.

Also we need to handle errors: if API fails, we need to retry once. If still fails, return error message.

We'll ask for missing latitude.
